change: Session-only undo. A document opens with nothing to undo (the closed-agent undo step and its history walk are gone), and a session that edited a document over 4 MiB closes with no history (Store::close_job trims straight to the latest version). Trimming while open is unchanged: past 16 MiB a checkpoint keeps the session's history when that fits, so a concurrent text edit can still branch from where the session opened.
why: Undo of an agent's edits made while a document was closed was the only reader of history kept across sessions. Dropping it removes the close-time session step and the open-time walk over agent commits.

storeCost.note: Medians on an otherwise idle machine; baseline is history-trimming-2026-10-02.json storeCost. Within run-to-run noise; neither changed path is on these measurements.

growth.note: Max saved bytes, the bound, is equal or lower for every template. Doodle Board's final size is one sample of a sawtooth that trims above 4 MiB, so it depends on where day 365 falls in the cycle. Flush times vary with machine load; the flush path did not change.
